summary:
ASTRO MISSION is an Artificial Intelligence (AI) simulator for astronaut training for kids aged 7-12 to make real space science fun for them. It turns space exploration into an interactive survival game, in which players are responsible for a settlement on the Moon or Mars, the health of the astronauts, oxygen, water, food and energy, as well as for responding to emergency situations like solar radiation storms, equipment failures or resource shortages.

It combines NASA data sources (DONKI, OSDR, BVAD, Mars RAD, and lunar terrain datasets), machine learning models, and a NASA-focused AI Mission Commander. Children learn about the actual functioning of space missions through interactive gameplay, 3D visualization of planets, predictions on resources, classification of the terrain, and educational quizzes.

One key innovation is transparent data provenance of distinguishing NASA observations, engineering baselines, synthetic calibrated data, and ML predictions. ASTRO MISSION makes science understandable, fostering the next generation of astronauts, engineers and scientists.
details:
ASTRO MISSION: AI-Powered Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

1. Introduction

ASTRO MISSION is an interactive astronaut training and space survival simulator designed for children aged 7–12. The project transforms complex space science into an engaging, hands-on learning experience.

Players take responsibility for managing a human settlement on the Moon (Shackleton Crater) or Mars (Jezero Crater). They must make decisions about limited resources, astronaut health, life-support systems, and unexpected emergencies.

Unlike traditional educational platforms that focus primarily on memorizing scientific facts, ASTRO MISSION teaches through practical decision-making. Every action has consequences, helping children understand the challenges of real human space exploration.

2. How the Application Works

The application provides several interactive modules:

Mission Control

  • Monitor the status of the space settlement.
  • Track oxygen, water, food, and energy supplies.
  • Monitor astronaut health and environmental conditions.
  • Advance through mission sols and observe resource consumption.

Base Builder

  • Construct and manage seven infrastructure modules.
  • Build greenhouses, power plants, laboratories, medical bays, storage facilities, communication systems, and living quarters.
  • Understand how infrastructure affects survival.

Radiation Predictor

  • Estimate radiation exposure and risk levels.
  • Use NASA Mars Radiation Assessment Detector data for scientific calibration.
  • Present radiation risk information through an interactive interface.

Resource Predictor

  • Estimate oxygen, water, food, and power requirements.
  • Incorporate NASA BVAD engineering baselines.
  • Compare model predictions with baseline calculations.

Terrain Classifier

  • Explore lunar surface terrain.
  • Classify crater-related terrain categories.
  • Incorporate a CNN trained using NASA JPL LROCNet imagery.

AI Mission Commander

  • Ask questions about space exploration, astronaut safety, and mission operations.
  • Retrieve relevant information from NASA technical documents using TF-IDF-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
  • Provide educational explanations and NASA references.

Science Center

  • Explore NASA datasets and scientific resources.
  • Understand the origin of observations, engineering baselines, and predictions.
  • Learn how scientific data supports space exploration.

Space Academy and Quiz

  • Access seven educational lessons.
  • Complete interactive quizzes.
  • Learn about radiation, life-support systems, planetary environments, and astronaut survival.

3. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning

ASTRO MISSION incorporates four AI/ML components:

  1. Radiation Risk Forecaster:
    Random Forest and Gradient Boosting models designed to estimate radiation exposure and risk levels.
  2. AI Mission Commander:
    A local TF-IDF-based RAG system that retrieves information from NASA knowledge documents and generates educational responses using templates.
  3. Resource Consumption Predictor:
    Four independent Random Forest regression models designed to estimate oxygen, water, food, and power requirements using NASA BVAD-calibrated scenarios.
  4. Lunar Terrain Classifier:
    A MobileNetV2 convolutional neural network trained using real NASA JPL LROCNet images, supported by morphological terrain classification.

The models were developed and evaluated during the project. However, some trained model artifacts are not currently loading in the production deployment, and the frontend uses fallback mechanisms for affected features.

4. NASA Data Integration

The project incorporates six NASA-related scientific data resources:

  • DONKI: Space weather events, solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and solar energetic particle events.
  • OSDR: Space biology and astronaut health research.
  • BVAD: Engineering baselines for human life-support requirements.
  • Mars RAD: Radiation measurements collected by the Curiosity rover.
  • LROCNet: Lunar surface imagery used for terrain classification.
  • RadLab: Radiation and dosimetry reference information.

These resources help connect gameplay mechanics with real scientific information.

5. Key Innovation: Transparent Data Provenance

One of the main innovations is the four-category data provenance system.

  • NASA_OBSERVATION: Information obtained from NASA observations and datasets.
  • NASA_ENGINEERING_BASELINE: Values derived from NASA engineering references.
  • SYNTHETIC_CALIBRATED: Synthetic training data calibrated using NASA scientific references.
  • ML_PREDICTION: Results generated by machine learning models.

This approach teaches children not only scientific concepts but also how to understand the origin and reliability of information.

6. Benefits and Intended Impact

For Children:

  • Develop critical thinking and decision-making skills.
  • Understand the relationship between life-support resources.
  • Learn about radiation and planetary environments.
  • Explore scientific concepts through interactive gameplay.
  • Develop an interest in STEM education.

For Educators:

  • Provide an interactive space science learning platform.
  • Introduce engineering concepts through practical scenarios.
  • Encourage problem-solving and systems thinking.
  • Support learning through quizzes and educational modules.

Intended Impact:

ASTRO MISSION aims to inspire the next generation of astronauts, engineers, scientists, and space researchers by making authentic space science accessible to younger learners.

It demonstrates that human space exploration requires scientific knowledge, engineering, resource management, teamwork, and responsible decision-making.

7. Technologies and Tools Used

Programming Languages:

  • Python 3.11
  • JavaScript ES6+
  • SQL

Frontend:

  • React 18
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Framer Motion
  • Three.js
  • Recharts

Backend:

  • Python FastAPI
  • SQLAlchemy
  • Pydantic
  • Uvicorn

AI and Machine Learning:

  • Scikit-learn
  • TensorFlow
  • NumPy
  • Pandas
  • TF-IDF Vectorization
  • Random Forest
  • Gradient Boosting
  • MobileNetV2 CNN

Database:

  • SQLite
  • PostgreSQL-compatible architecture

Deployment:

  • AWS CloudFront
  • AWS EC2
  • Caddy Reverse Proxy

Testing:

  • Playwright
  • Pytest
  • Automated ML testing

8. Creativity and Innovation

ASTRO MISSION combines interactive gaming, NASA scientific resources, machine learning, and educational storytelling into one platform.

Its major creative elements include:

  • Interactive Moon and Mars settlement management.
  • Three-dimensional planetary visualization using Three.js.
  • Realistic resource management and survival scenarios.
  • AI-powered NASA knowledge retrieval.
  • Machine learning-based scientific prediction components.
  • Transparent scientific data provenance.
  • Emergency scenarios involving radiation storms, oxygen leaks, water recycling failures, and power outages.

The platform encourages children to experience the complexity of space exploration rather than simply read about it.

9. Factors Considered During Development

Scientific Accuracy:
NASA scientific datasets and engineering references were considered when designing resource management and radiation-related calculations.

Age-Appropriate Design:
The interface uses visual indicators, accessible controls, interactive gameplay, and educational explanations suitable for children aged 7–12.

Accessibility:
The application is browser-based and responsive across mobile, tablet, and desktop devices.

Educational Value:
The project focuses on practical understanding, critical thinking, systems engineering, and scientific literacy.

Performance:
Frontend fallback mechanisms allow several educational and gameplay features to remain usable when backend services are unavailable.

10. Conclusion

ASTRO MISSION bridges the gap between classroom science and real-world space exploration.

By combining NASA data, interactive simulations, AI-assisted learning, and resource management challenges, the project creates an engaging environment where children can experience the responsibilities of managing a human settlement beyond Earth.

Our vision is to make the next generation curious about space, confident in science, and prepared to solve the engineering challenges of future lunar and Martian exploration.
